svg.aria-label: buildermesh across three boxes, in five scenes: every box builds at once; a coordinator on hub-box follows leads on every box through the NATS hub and holds one before it lands until another has landed, and the held lead's daemon wakes it on release; a lead queues a check that needs macOS and the laptop's daemon takes it; leads' finishes, asks and blocks reach your phone as push notifications; after a change lands, bmesh sync levels every box's checkout, and the sleeping laptop levels when it wakes
svg.title: buildermesh across boxes
svg.text: hub-box runs the hub; build-box dials it; the laptop's leaf relays to it. On every box, bmesh serve is always on.

g.text: Each box runs its own leads and executors through its own runner,
each in its own git worktree, all at once.
2. A coordinator keeps leads on every box in step.
Your coordinator session starts leads on all three boxes and follows their events through the hub.
It holds app-012 before it lands until api-007 has landed, then releases it,
and build-box's daemon wakes app-012 to go on.
3. A lead sends a check to the box that can run it.
app-012 queues xcode, a kind with os = "darwin". The job waits on the hub
until the laptop's daemon, on the one Mac, takes it and runs it;
the result comes back to app-012 as a reply.
When a lead is done, asks or is blocked, its event goes through the hub
to the daemon with ntfy set, which pushes it to your phone, once.
5. A change that lands reaches every box.
app-012 lands, which moves build-box's checkout. You run bmesh sync: it levels hub-box
and sends each other box's daemon a level job; build-box's answers with a reply, the asleep laptop's is queued.
When the laptop wakes it levels, holds a new plugins commit for your approval, and leaves its reply on the hub.
every box builds; a coordinator keeps leads in step; a check goes to the box that can run it;
push notifications reach your phone; a change that lands reaches every box.
bmesh hub · relays to the hub
